Approval requires sign-off from the system's data owner and two engineering managers, with one manager from a different team than the requesting engineer [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. All approvals must be recorded in the form, and requesting engineers must have completed annual security training within the last ninety days [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. For emergencies during an incident, an on-call engineer may use break-glass access without waiting for standard approval [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13].

attempts.answer_text: The Production Database Access SOP describes the operational steps for how an engineer requests, receives, and loses production database access [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. It applies to every engineer needing direct read or write access to a production database, such as on-call engineers, those debugging customer issues, or running one-time data migrations [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. Engineers request access via the internal tools portal form, which requires sign-off from the data owner and two engineering managers (one from a different team) [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. Approved access is granted for three days and expires automatically [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. Engineers must have completed annual security training within the last ninety days [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. During an incident, on-call engineers can request break-glass emergency access without standard approval [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13]. All access grants are logged and reviewed weekly by Security Engineering [da1cdb5e0e87ad69728e9d2781239d13], and access can be revoked early by either approver or the data owner [91d4f121536a0880dff84e83193cd833]. Service accounts and automated jobs follow a separate process requiring data owner and two manager sign-offs, with standing access reviewed quarterly [91d4f121536a0880dff84e83193cd833].
